problems.title: Reward support does not imply ratio closeness
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v2 Appendix A, PDF p.17, Lemma A.1 and Assumption A.2
claim: After Lemma A.1, the paper infers Assumption A.2, including \(|\pi_\theta(y)/\mu(y)-1|\leq\delta\), from its rewarded-support construction.
analysis: Behavior probabilities \((0.99,0.01)\) and target probabilities \((0.01,0.99)\) have identical positive support. Reward only the shorter correct first output. The rewarded ratio is \(1/99\), with deviation \(98/99\) from one, despite satisfying the support requirement. Caption success or positive support does not impose a numerical ratio bound.
result: The support-to-closeness implication fails. The scalar lemma remains valid if closeness is supplied separately.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Assume or assess ratio closeness independently. With \(|R|\leq1\), that premise gives \(|\mathbb E[(w-1)R]|\leq\delta\), but does not itself control policy-gradient error.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a supporting assumption inference; the separate gradient counterexample establishes the central damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The ratio-free update can oppose the true return gradient
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v2 Section 4.3, PDF p.5, Eq.(7); Appendix A, PDF pp.17–18, Lemma A.3
claim: Equation (7) cites a scalar importance-sampling lemma when replacing the weighted policy-gradient expectation by an unweighted one.
analysis: Use two equally likely contexts with behavior reward probability \(1/2\). Target reward probabilities are \(p_A=0.505+2\theta\), \(p_B=0.495-1.98\theta\), for \(|\theta|\leq1/400\). All rewarded ratios are within \(0.02\) of one. At zero, the true expected-return derivative is \((2-1.98)/2=1/100\). The ratio-free score expectation is \([2/0.505-1.98/0.495]/4=-1/101\). Thus even the assumed small ratios permit an update opposite to return improvement; equality of scalar objectives at the point does not control their derivatives.
result: The derivation of the core ratio-free return gradient is invalid under the stated assumptions. Empirical usefulness of reward-weighted likelihood is a different claim.
assumptions: The fixed data law has two equally likely contexts, bounded binary rewards and the stated near-unit rewarded importance ratios.
repair: Retain importance weights, or state a gradient-specific bound. If rewarded score norm is bounded by \(M\), error is at most \(\delta\mathbb E[|R|\|s\|]\leq\delta M\). Alternatively identify the update as the gradient of a fixed-data reward-weighted log-likelihood objective.
problems.impact_rationale: This directly contradicts the central policy-gradient justification, even after granting its ratio-closeness premise.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Selected GRPO checkpoints reuse reported evaluation scores
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v2 Section 6.2, PDF p.7, checkpoint-selection paragraph; evaluation appendix
claim: Section 6.2 selects GRPO checkpoints by average MathVision/MMMU Pro performance and then reports those benchmarks; Appendix C identifies the evaluation splits.
analysis: Those outcomes are therefore model-selection data for the selected GRPO rows, rather than an untouched final test. The selection rule does not establish training-data overlap, a numerical optimism magnitude or a ranking reversal. SOPHIA-only rows outside that selection are not implicated.
result: The relevant benchmark rows need a selection-aware interpretation. Their reported values are not recalculated.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use a disjoint validation set or a prespecified step, then assess the selected checkpoint on independent test data. Existing checkpoints may permit a new evaluation without retraining.
problems.impact_rationale: The protocol establishes reuse, but not a large quantified effect on the central comparison.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
